problem: Cut peak-hour traffic in the city centre by 25 to 30 percent.
title: Singapore introduces the world's first area licensing scheme for the city centre
context: Traffic in the central business district was congested.
decision_made: Charge a supplementary licence fee to enter a restricted central zone.
action_taken: Launched on 2 June 1975, using manual enforcement and a flat fee, and replaced by Electronic Road Pricing on 1 April 1998.
observed_outcome: Reports say the scheme virtually eliminated congestion inside the zone. After ERP, weekday traffic entering the zone fell 24 percent and speeds rose from 30-35 to 40-45 km/h. A 45 percent early reduction in one factsheet was not verified.
lessons: Road pricing can cut congestion, but a flat fee and manual enforcement limited the first design.
limitations: Figures are from secondary sources and the primary studies were not checked. The flat fee did not account for multiple trips per day.

claims.claim_text: Singapore launched the Area Licensing Scheme on 2 June 1975, charging drivers to enter a restricted central zone.
Electronic Road Pricing reduced traffic in the restricted zone and gave more reliable travel times.
